#: Default per-turn resolve budget. Overridable per scope: the point of a budget is
#: that a host can make it small, and a runaway loop then fails by name instead of
#: quietly costing a context window.
DEFAULT_MAX_REFS = 64


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scope:
    """The capability scope a session presents on every resolve.

    It carries the index (which is what the session is allowed to name), the
    enumerated projections, the resolve budget and the block size. A scope is
    neither a user nor a token: it is the grant, and ``scope.name`` must equal the
    name the index was compiled under.
    """

    name: str
    index: TurnIndex
    projections: Optional[Mapping[str, Iterable[str]]] = None
    max_refs: int = DEFAULT_MAX_REFS
    block_size: Optional[int] = field(default=None)

    def block(self) -> int:
        """The cache block granularity this scope resolves against."""
        return self.block_size if self.block_size is not None else self.index.block_size

    def enumerated(self, kind: str) -> frozenset[str]:
        return projections_for(kind, self.projections)


def _refuse(ledger: Optional[Ledger], scope_name: str, text: str, error: PtrError) -> None:
    """Record the refusal before re-raising. A refusal is a measurement too."""
    if ledger is not None:
        ledger.record_refusal(
            scope=scope_name, serialized_ref=text, code=error.code
        )


def resolve(
    ref: Reference,
    scope: Scope,
    ledger: Optional[Ledger] = None,
) -> ResourceRef:
    """Resolve ``ref`` within ``scope``, recording exactly one ledger row.

    Raises a named error for every refusal; the refusal is recorded in the ledger
    first, with ``refs_refused=1``.
    """
    if not isinstance(ref, Reference):
        raise PtrNotAReferenceError(
            "resolve() takes a Reference; a ResourceRef is content identity and "
            f"cannot be resolved, got {type(ref).__name__}",
            got=type(ref).__name__,
        )
    if not isinstance(scope, Scope):
        raise PtrScopeUngrantedError(
            "resolve() takes a Scope; no capability was presented",
            got=type(scope).__name__,
        )

    presented = format_ref(ref)
    try:
        if scope.index.scope != scope.name:
            raise PtrScopeUngrantedError(
                f"this index was compiled under scope {scope.index.scope!r}, "
                f"the session presents {scope.name!r}",
                index_scope=scope.index.scope,
                presented=scope.name,
            )
        if ref.kind not in REF_KINDS:
            raise PtrUnknownKindError(f"unknown kind {ref.kind!r}", kind=ref.kind)

        entry = scope.index.entries.get((ref.kind, ref.id))
        if entry is None:
            raise PtrUnknownIdError(
                f"the index enumerates no {ref.kind}:{ref.id}",
                kind=ref.kind,
                id=ref.id,
                enumerated=sorted(f"{k}:{i}" for k, i in scope.index.entries),
            )

        if ref.revision is not None and ref.revision != scope.index.revision:
            raise PtrRevisionError(
                f"{presented} pins revision {ref.revision}; this index is "
                f"revision {scope.index.revision}",
                pinned=ref.revision,
                index_revision=scope.index.revision,
            )

        if ref.projection is not None and ref.projection not in scope.enumerated(ref.kind):
            raise PtrProjectionUngrantedError(
                f"projection {ref.projection!r} is not enumerated for kind "
                f"{ref.kind!r}; enumerated: {sorted(scope.enumerated(ref.kind))}",
                kind=ref.kind,
                projection=ref.projection,
            )

        if ref.pointer is not None and ref.pointer not in entry.regions:
            raise PtrPointerError(
                f"{ref.kind}:{ref.id} exposes no region at {ref.pointer!r}",
                kind=ref.kind,
                id=ref.id,
                pointer=ref.pointer,
            )

        if ledger is not None and ledger.resolved_count() >= scope.max_refs:
            raise PtrBudgetExceededError(
                f"resolve budget spent: {ledger.resolved_count()} of "
                f"{scope.max_refs} refs this turn",
                max_refs=scope.max_refs,
                resolved=ledger.resolved_count(),
            )

        target: ResourceRef = (
            entry.regions.get(ref.pointer, entry.target)
            if ref.pointer is not None
            else entry.target
        )
    except PtrError as error:
        _refuse(ledger, scope.name, presented, error)
        raise

    if ledger is not None:
        ledger.record_resolution(
            scope=scope.name,
            serialized_ref=presented,
            bytes_appended=len(presented.encode("utf-8")),
            block_size=scope.block(),
            entry_text=entry.text,
        )
    return target

class PtrError(Exception):
    """Base of every engine error. ``code`` is stable; treat it as API."""

    code = "PTR_ERROR"

    def __init__(self, detail: str = "", **context: Any) -> None:
        self.detail = detail
        self.context = dict(context)
        msg = f"{self.code}: {detail}" if detail else self.code
        super().__init__(msg)

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"code": self.code, "detail": self.detail, "context": self.context}


class PtrSyntaxError(PtrError):
    """The token is not of the form ``@kind:id[#pointer][@revision][?projection]``."""

    code = "PTR_SYNTAX"


class PtrUnknownKindError(PtrError):
    """``kind`` is not one of the enumerated kinds (Duval D-024 / ``REF_KINDS``)."""

    code = "PTR_UNKNOWN_KIND"


class PtrUnknownIdError(PtrError):
    """The id is well formed but this index enumerates no such item."""

    code = "PTR_UNKNOWN_ID"


class PtrScopeUngrantedError(PtrError):
    """The presented capability scope did not compile this index."""

    code = "PTR_SCOPE_UNGRANTED"


class PtrProjectionUngrantedError(PtrError):
    """The requested projection is not enumerated for that kind."""

    code = "PTR_PROJECTION_UNENUMERATED"


class PtrPointerError(PtrError):
    """The JSON pointer is malformed, or selects no region in the item body."""

    code = "PTR_POINTER_INVALID"


class PtrBudgetExceededError(PtrError):
    """The per-turn resolve budget (``Scope.max_refs``) is spent."""

    code = "PTR_BUDGET_EXCEEDED"


class PtrRevisionError(PtrError):
    """The reference pins a revision the index was not compiled at."""

    code = "PTR_REVISION_MISMATCH"


class PtrHashMismatchError(PtrError):
    """Bytes read back are not the bytes the content identity names."""

    code = "PTR_HASH_MISMATCH"


class PtrStoreMissError(PtrError):
    """The content identity names a body that is not in the store."""

    code = "PTR_STORE_MISS"


class PtrWarmpoolViolationError(PtrError):
    """The store root resolves inside the repository working tree."""

    code = "PTR_WARMPOOL_INSIDE_REPO"


class PtrExtensionError(PtrError):
    """A body extension is not a plain dotted suffix."""

    code = "PTR_EXTENSION_INVALID"


class PtrDuplicateIdError(PtrError):
    """Two items in one turn claim the same ``(kind, id)``."""

    code = "PTR_DUPLICATE_ID"


class PtrMaterialError(PtrError):
    """A material item is missing a required field or has the wrong type."""

    code = "PTR_MATERIAL_INVALID"


class PtrNotAReferenceError(PtrError):
    """A resolver was handed something that is not a ``Reference``."""

    code = "PTR_NOT_A_REFERENCE"


class PtrUnresolvedRefError(PtrError):
    """The adapter was handed a ref that was not explicitly resolved."""

    code = "PTR_UNRESOLVED_REF"


class PtrBodyMismatchError(PtrError):
    """Body bytes handed to the adapter are not the bytes that ref resolved to."""

    code = "PTR_BODY_MISMATCH"


class PtrTokenSourceRequiredError(PtrError):
    """Token counts were supplied without naming where they came from.

    A count with no provenance is indistinguishable from a measurement, and this
    project has already paid for a zero that meant "unknown".
    """

    code = "PTR_TOKEN_SOURCE_REQUIRED"


class PtrAnnotationError(PtrError):
    """An annotation was asked for something it cannot annotate."""

    code = "PTR_ANNOTATION_INVALID"


__all__ = [
    "PtrError",
    "PtrSyntaxError",
    "PtrUnknownKindError",
    "PtrUnknownIdError",
    "PtrScopeUngrantedError",
    "PtrProjectionUngrantedError",
    "PtrPointerError",
    "PtrBudgetExceededError",
    "PtrRevisionError",
    "PtrHashMismatchError",
    "PtrStoreMissError",
    "PtrWarmpoolViolationError",
    "PtrExtensionError",
    "PtrDuplicateIdError",
    "PtrMaterialError",
    "PtrNotAReferenceError",
    "PtrUnresolvedRefError",
    "PtrBodyMismatchError",
    "PtrTokenSourceRequiredError",
    "PtrAnnotationError",
    "PtrLawError",
    "PtrLawUnknownServerError",
    "PtrLawBoundInvalidError",
    "PtrLawSeriesLengthError",
    "PtrLawObservedInvalidError",
]

class PtrLedgerError(PtrError, ValueError):
    """A ledger row or counter was supplied in a shape the row contract refuses.

    Also a ``ValueError`` so callers written before the code existed (and
    ``tests/test_ledger.py``'s refusal test) keep catching it -- the code is the
    improvement, the exception family is not a break.
    """

    code = "PTR_LEDGER_ERROR"


class PtrLedgerCountError(PtrLedgerError):
    """A counter (``refs_resolved``, ``bytes_appended``, ...) is not a non-negative int."""

    code = "PTR_LEDGER_COUNT"


class PtrLedgerBlockSizeError(PtrLedgerError):
    """``block_size`` is not a positive int."""

    code = "PTR_LEDGER_BLOCK_SIZE"


class PtrLedgerIdError(PtrLedgerError):
    """``ledger_id`` is not a non-empty string."""

    code = "PTR_LEDGER_ID"


class PtrLedgerScopeError(PtrLedgerError):
    """``scope`` is not a non-empty string."""

    code = "PTR_LEDGER_SCOPE"


class PtrLedgerRefusalCodeError(PtrLedgerError):
    """A refusal row's ``code`` is not a named ``PTR_*`` code."""

    code = "PTR_LEDGER_REFUSAL_CODE"


class PtrLawError(PtrLedgerError):
    """A hit-ledger (billing law) call was handed something the law cannot read.

    Same exception family as the ledger errors -- a ``PtrError`` that is also a
    ``ValueError`` -- so a caller written before the codes existed still catches it.
    The codes live in ``LEDGER_LAW_CODES``, not in ``LEDGER_CODES``: the five ledger
    codes are the row contract's, and these four are the law's.
    """

    code = "PTR_LAW_ERROR"


class PtrLawUnknownServerError(PtrLawError):
    """The named server has no measured cache profile, so no prediction is possible."""

    code = "PTR_LAW_UNKNOWN_SERVER"


class PtrLawBoundInvalidError(PtrLawError):
    """``P1``/``L``/an observed count is not a non-negative int (or ``None`` where allowed)."""

    code = "PTR_LAW_BOUND_INVALID"


class PtrLawSeriesLengthError(PtrLawError):
    """The supplied observed series does not line up one-to-one with the recorded turns."""

    code = "PTR_LAW_SERIES_LENGTH"


class PtrLawObservedInvalidError(PtrLawError):
    """An observed series entry is malformed, or contradicts the turn it is applied to."""

    code = "PTR_LAW_OBSERVED_INVALID"

def test_the_wrong_scope_is_ungranted(index, ledger):
    other = Scope(name="sess-02", index=index)
    with pytest.raises(PtrScopeUngrantedError) as excinfo:
        resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@3"), other, ledger)
    assert excinfo.value.code == "PTR_SCOPE_UNGRANTED"
    assert ledger.rows[-1]["refs_refused"] == 1
    assert ledger.resolved_count() == 0


def test_the_right_scope_resolves(index, ledger):
    scope = Scope(name="sess-01", index=index)
    target = resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@3"), scope, ledger)
    assert target.hash.startswith("sha256:")
    assert ledger.resolved_count() == 1


def test_a_scope_must_be_presented_not_implied(index):
    with pytest.raises(PtrScopeUngrantedError):
        resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@3"), "sess-01", None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_an_unknown_id_is_refused_by_name(index, ledger):
    scope = Scope(name="sess-01", index=index)
    with pytest.raises(PtrUnknownIdError) as excinfo:
        resolve(parse("@knowledge:k99@3"), scope, ledger)
    assert excinfo.value.code == "PTR_UNKNOWN_ID"
    assert "knowledge:k01" in excinfo.value.context["enumerated"]


def test_a_ref_pinned_to_another_revision_is_refused(index, ledger):
    scope = Scope(name="sess-01", index=index)
    with pytest.raises(PtrRevisionError) as excinfo:
        resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@9"), scope, ledger)
    assert excinfo.value.code == "PTR_REVISION_MISMATCH"
    assert excinfo.value.context["pinned"] == 9
    assert excinfo.value.context["index_revision"] == 3


def test_a_ref_with_no_revision_resolves_at_head(index, ledger):
    scope = Scope(name="sess-01", index=index)
    assert resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01"), scope, ledger).digest
    assert ledger.resolved_count() == 1


def test_the_budget_is_per_turn_and_configurable(index, ledger):
    scope = Scope(name="sess-01", index=index, max_refs=2)
    resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@3"), scope, ledger)
    resolve(parse("@knowledge:k02@3"), scope, ledger)
    with pytest.raises(PtrBudgetExceededError) as excinfo:
        resolve(parse("@knowledge:k03@3"), scope, ledger)
    assert excinfo.value.code == "PTR_BUDGET_EXCEEDED"
    assert excinfo.value.context["max_refs"] == 2
    assert len(ledger) == 3
    assert ledger.resolved_count() == 2
    assert ledger.refused_count() == 1


def test_a_bigger_budget_admits_more(index, ledger):
    scope = Scope(name="sess-01", index=index, max_refs=5)
    for text in index.texts()[:5]:
        resolve(parse(text), scope, ledger)
    assert ledger.resolved_count() == 5

def test_all_seven_codes_are_distinct(index, ledger):
    codes: list[str] = []
    cases = [
        (lambda: parse("knowledge:k01"), None),
        (lambda: parse("@widget:k01"), None),
        (lambda: resolve(parse("@knowledge:nope@3"), Scope("sess-01", index), ledger), None),
        (lambda: resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@3"), Scope("sess-99", index), ledger), None),
        (
            lambda: resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@3?secret-view"), Scope("sess-01", index), ledger),
            None,
        ),
        (lambda: resolve(parse("@artifact:plan#/nope@3"), Scope("sess-01", index), ledger), None),
    ]
    for case, _ in cases:
        with pytest.raises(PtrError) as excinfo:
            case()
        codes.append(excinfo.value.code)

    tight = Scope("sess-01", index, max_refs=1)
    resolve(parse("@knowledge:k01@3"), tight, ledger)
    with pytest.raises(PtrError) as excinfo:
        resolve(parse("@knowledge:k02@3"), tight, ledger)
    codes.append(excinfo.value.code)

    assert len(codes) == 7
    assert len(set(codes)) == 7, f"two controls collapsed onto one code: {codes}"
    assert codes == [
        "PTR_SYNTAX",
        "PTR_UNKNOWN_KIND",
        "PTR_UNKNOWN_ID",
        "PTR_SCOPE_UNGRANTED",
        "PTR_PROJECTION_UNENUMERATED",
        "PTR_POINTER_INVALID",
        "PTR_BUDGET_EXCEEDED",
    ]

You are a long-horizon coding agent working on the ptr-engine acceptance target. Work only from the pinned working set shown to you; obey every negative constraint; never claim a command you did not run, and never restate a fact you did not read.

ANSWER BUDGET (bounded tier, fixture_version v2-bounded). Every answer is measured in words and the count is recorded, not truncated and not re-prompted. Budgets are per turn: at most 150 words on a work, plant, or repair turn; at most 400 words on a checkpoint or verify turn. Your own answer text is the only thing counted, and any code or log you quote inside the answer counts toward it. Give the result and the single line of evidence that establishes it; do not re-quote source you did not change, do not restate the plan, do not summarise earlier turns. At a checkpoint turn the grader compares your ENTIRE answer with the value it expects, so answer with the value alone: no units, no restated question, no commentary, unless the question asks for a phrase or a list. At a verify turn you must still name the test files you ran, their exit status, and every count the task asks for. If a fact does not fit the budget, cut narration, never the fact: an answer that omits a required fact to stay under budget has failed the task. ANSWER CONTRACT (fixture v5; normative, and it supersedes every earlier ANSWER instruction).
The checkpoint question arrives at named turns: T6, T8, T12, T14, T18, T20, T24, T26, T32, T36, T42, T46 (12 checkpoints, one per turn). On those turns the tools are unavailable - no read_file, no fetch, no follow-up request is served, so answer only from what is already in front of you. On a checkpoint turn emit exactly ONE line and nothing else, in one of these four forms:
  ANSWER: NUM <integer>
  ANSWER: CALL <callee>(<kw>=<value>, <kw>=<value>, ...)
  ANSWER: NONE
  ANSWER: TEXT <one line of prose>
For CALL, give the keyword arguments in alphabetical order, and give each value as the source text shows it. A citation written after the value is allowed and is not the value: `ANSWER: 6 (scope.py:3)` reads as the number 6. Anything that is not one of the four forms is a failed checkpoint. TEXT is accepted structurally and is never graded as a pass. On a work, plant or repair turn the budget above still applies and the last line of the answer must be this contract line whenever the turn asks a checkpoint question; a work-turn answer needs no ANSWER line.
